questions.question: Dad swipes his debit card at the store. What is he doing?
questions.explain: Swiping a debit card is paying. It uses your own money from the bank, so it is not free.

questions.question: You send an e-transfer to pay for a $20 cake. Is that paying?
questions.explain: An e-transfer sends real money, so it is paying. It is not free, and it is not a trade.

questions.question: Sam gives his old skateboard for a new one. What is that called?
questions.explain: Giving one thing for another is trading. It is a real way to pay, just not with money.

questions.question: At the farmers' market, you want to buy $10 of strawberries. You can pay with bills, a card, or an e-transfer. Which are real ways to pay?
questions.explain: Bills, a card, and an e-transfer are all real ways to pay. Each one uses your own money.

questions.question: At the used-toy shop, you can pay $15 in cash OR trade your old toy. Are both real ways to pay?
questions.explain: Cash and trading are both real ways to pay. Neither one is free, and neither is the only option.

questions.question: Your friend says, 'You can only pay with coins and bills. Cards do not count as paying.' Is your friend right?
options: Yes, only cash is real money
No, cards are a way to pay
questions.explain: A debit card uses your own bank money, so it is real paying. It is not free, and cash is not the only way.

questions.question: Lily pays for a pizza with a card, and Sam pays for one with cash. Tom says, 'Lily did not really pay.' Mia says, 'Only Sam really paid.' Who is wrong?
options: Tom is right about the card
Tom and Mia are both wrong
Mia is right about the cash
questions.explain: A card is real paying, and cash is real paying. Tom and Mia are both wrong to say one does not count.

questions.question: You earn $15 washing your bike. You spend $5 on a snack with a card. You trade your old cap for a new one. Is the card spending real paying?
options: No, the card money was free
No, only the cash is real
No, trading is the only pay
Yes, it used your own money
questions.explain: A debit card takes money from your own account, so it is real paying. It does not cost you nothing.

questions.question: Mom taps her bank card to buy milk. Whose money pays for the milk?
questions.explain: A bank card takes real money out of Mom's own account. Paying by card is not free money.

questions.question: Kim sends $10 by e-transfer to pay her aunt. Does the $10 leave Kim's account?
questions.explain: An e-transfer moves real money out of Kim's account. It counts as paying, just like cash.

questions.question: Ali pays for shoes with a credit card. Is a credit card a way to pay?
questions.explain: A credit card pays the store now, and Ali pays the bank back later. That is real paying, not free money.

questions.question: Ella hands the clerk a $5 bill for a pen. Which way to pay is she using?
questions.explain: Bills and coins are cash, so Ella is paying with cash. Cards and e-transfers do not use bills.

questions.question: Maya's grandma lives far away in Kelowna. Maya wants to send her $20 today. Which way to pay works best?
questions.explain: An e-transfer sends real money to someone far away in minutes. Cash and trades need you to be there in person.

questions.question: At the book fair, Ana pays $6 with her mom's debit card. Ana says the book was free. Why is Ana wrong?
questions.explain: Mom's card moved $6 out of her account, so the book was not free. A card still costs real money.

questions.question: The food truck sign says cash or card only. Noah has $4 cash, a bus pass, and a toy to trade. How can Noah pay?
questions.explain: This truck takes only cash or a card, so Noah uses his $4 cash. Trading and e-transfer are real ways to pay, but not here.

questions.question: Sam pays for skates with an e-transfer. His friend asks if Sam still has that money. What is true?
questions.explain: The e-transfer moved Sam's real money to the shop, so it is gone from his account. E-transfer money is not free.

questions.question: Jo has $30 in her account. She pays $8 by debit for a book. Then she pays $5 by debit for socks. How much is left?
questions.explain: Debit takes real money out both times: 30 take away 8 is 22, then 22 take away 5 is 17. The account does not stay at $30 just because she used a card.

questions.question: Ravi had $25 in his account. He paid for a hat with his debit card. Now he has $18. What did the hat cost?
questions.explain: Find the missing part: 25 take away 18 is 7. The card did not make the hat free.

questions.question: Ava has $16 in her account. She pays $9 by e-transfer for a ticket. Her brother says she still has $16 because no coins moved. How much does Ava really have?
questions.explain: An e-transfer really takes money out: 16 take away 9 is 7. No coins moved, but the money still left her account.

questions.question: Ken has $10 in his account. He pays $10 by card for a game. He says his card is free, so he still has $10. What is wrong with what Ken says?
options: He paid nothing for the game
The card gave him free money
questions.explain: The card took $10 out of his account, so Ken now has $0. Paying by card is never free.
